selection_reasons.type: The page is a documented example of work, approach and outcomes, matching the case study definition.
selection_reasons.audiences: The content is aimed at developers using the frameworks, documentation managers overseeing documentation strategy, and technical writers creating similar documentation.
selection_reasons.topics: The page covers API documentation for Scala frameworks, developer experience through improved documentation, information architecture via structured outlines, and technical writing practice.
selection_reasons.technologies: Scala, C++, JVM, JNI, Kafka, Optimus and RICE are materially used and documented in the case study.
selection_reasons.lifecycle: The content represents current practice and portfolio material.

proposed_taxonomy_terms.label: JVM
proposed_taxonomy_terms.description: The Java Virtual Machine, a runtime environment for executing Java and other JVM languages such as Scala.
proposed_taxonomy_terms.reason: The JVM is a foundational runtime platform materially referenced in the document as part of the technology stack, but no existing term accurately represents it.
evidence: This required a strong understanding of Scala, C++, JVM/native interoperability and bitemporal database concepts.

proposed_taxonomy_terms.label: JNI
proposed_taxonomy_terms.description: Java Native Interface, a framework for interoperability between Java and native code.
proposed_taxonomy_terms.reason: JNI is a specific interoperability technology materially documented in the case study, and no existing term covers it.
evidence: Created developer documentation covering integration between Scala and native C++ code through JNI-based mechanisms, explaining cross-language interaction from the perspective of Scala developers.

proposed_taxonomy_terms.label: Optimus
proposed_taxonomy_terms.description: A Scala-based framework for building reactive user interfaces and data processing applications.
proposed_taxonomy_terms.reason: Optimus is a significant framework documented in the case study, and no existing term represents it.
evidence: Alongside leading the development of Morgan Stanley's new [custom docs-as-code platform](ScalingADeveloperDocsPlatform.md), I served as the lead and sole technical writer for the Optimus and RICE frameworks.

proposed_taxonomy_terms.label: RICE
proposed_taxonomy_terms.description: An internal framework for regression testing and data ingestion at Morgan Stanley.
proposed_taxonomy_terms.reason: RICE is a framework documented in the case study, and no existing term represents it.
evidence: Alongside leading the development of Morgan Stanley's new [custom docs-as-code platform](ScalingADeveloperDocsPlatform.md), I served as the lead and sole technical writer for the Optimus and RICE frameworks.

proposed_taxonomy_terms.label: Kafka
proposed_taxonomy_terms.reason: Kafka is materially used for event-stream processing in the Backfiller framework, and no existing term covers it.
evidence: Documented historical data backfilling, Kafka-based event-stream processing and writing external data into a bitemporal data store.

current_metadata.title: Documenting Complex Enterprise Developer Frameworks
current_metadata.description: How I reverse-engineered and documented complex Scala frameworks at Morgan Stanley, covering UI development, testing, interoperability and data ingestion.

caseStudyCard.description: Reverse-engineering and documenting complex Scala-based frameworks for enterprise software engineers
highlights: Lead technical writing for Optimus and RICE frameworks
Source-code analysis and reverse engineering of undocumented APIs
SME interviews and consolidation of legacy documentation
Scala code examples, compilation and technical validation
Reactive UI, regression testing, interoperability and data ingestion
